questions.title: The follicular phase of the ovarian cycle coincides with which of the following?
questions.question: The follicular phase of the ovarian cycle coincides with which of the following?

options.A: Proliferative phase of the uterine cycle
options.B: Secretory phase of the uterine cycle
options.C: Menstrual phase of the uterine cycle
options.D: Luteal phase of the uterine cycle

explanations.A: Correct. The follicular phase of the ovarian cycle, during which a dominant follicle matures under rising FSH and estrogen, runs in parallel with the proliferative phase of the uterine cycle, in which that same rising estrogen drives regrowth of the endometrium. Both phases are driven by the same rising follicular estrogen, which is why they are named for parallel, hormonally linked events in the ovary and uterus respectively.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The secretory phase of the uterine cycle corresponds to the luteal, not the follicular, phase of the ovarian cycle, driven by post-ovulatory progesterone.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The menstrual phase marks the very start of a new cycle, overlapping only the earliest days of the follicular phase, not the whole follicular phase.
explanations.D: Incorrect. "Luteal phase" is itself the ovarian-cycle term paired with the uterine secretory phase; it is not a named phase of the uterine cycle and does not correspond to the follicular phase.

questions.subject: gyn
questions.learning_objective: The follicular (ovarian) phase corresponds to the proliferative (uterine) phase.

questions.title: Which of the following is an effect of testosterone, via its conversion to dihydrotestosterone, on the male fetus?
questions.question: Which of the following is an effect of testosterone, via its conversion to dihydrotestosterone, on the male fetus?

options.B: Development of the uterus and fallopian tubes from the Müllerian ducts
options.D: Formation of the labia majora and minora

explanations.A: Correct. Testosterone is converted by 5-alpha reductase to dihydrotestosterone (DHT) in genital skin, and DHT drives masculinization of the external genitalia, transforming the genital tubercle, folds, and swellings into the penis and scrotum rather than the female-pattern default structures. Wolffian duct structures such as the epididymis and vas deferens, by contrast, are maintained directly by testosterone itself rather than by its DHT metabolite.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Development of the uterus and fallopian tubes from the Müllerian ducts is the female default pathway that occurs in the absence of Müllerian-inhibiting hormone, not an effect of testosterone.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Testosterone maintains and virilizes the Wolffian ducts into the epididymis, vas deferens, and seminal vesicles; it does not cause their regression.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The labia majora and minora are the female-pattern structures that form from the same embryonic swellings and folds in the absence of DHT, not because of testosterone/DHT action.

questions.learning_objective: Testosterone, via DHT, masculinizes the external genitalia, distinct from its direct maintenance of the Wolffian ducts.

questions.title: Which of the following is an effect of placental estrogen in late pregnancy?
questions.question: Which of the following is an effect of placental estrogen in late pregnancy?

options.B: Decreases myometrial excitability, maintaining uterine quiescence
options.D: Inhibits development of the mammary ductal system

explanations.A: Correct. Placental estrogen upregulates myometrial oxytocin receptors and gap junctions in late pregnancy, increasing uterine muscle excitability and coordination between muscle fibers, helping prepare the uterus for effective contractions at labor. Progesterone opposes this effect for most of pregnancy, so the shift toward estrogen dominance near term is part of what helps the uterus become primed for labor.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Maintaining uterine quiescence by decreasing myometrial excitability is progesterone's role throughout most of pregnancy, not estrogen's role in late pregnancy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Estrogen actually stimulates pituitary lactotroph proliferation and prolactin secretion during pregnancy, rather than suppressing it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Estrogen stimulates, rather than inhibits, proliferation of the mammary ductal system during pregnancy, in preparation for lactation.

questions.learning_objective: Placental estrogen raises myometrial excitability in late pregnancy, opposing progesterone's quiescence effect.

questions.title: Which of the following is true concerning human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)?
questions.question: Which of the following is true concerning human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)?

options.A: It appears in maternal blood approximately 6 days after conception
options.B: It is first detectable only after the first missed menstrual period
options.C: It is synthesized exclusively by the maternal corpus luteum
options.D: It shares no structural homology with pituitary LH

explanations.A: Correct. hCG, secreted by the syncytiotrophoblast of the implanting blastocyst, appears in maternal blood approximately six days after conception, around the time of implantation, and its detection is what allows sensitive pregnancy tests to be positive before a missed period. The alpha subunit hCG shares with LH is also why hCG can cross-react in some older LH assays and why it can bind and stimulate the LH receptor to sustain the corpus luteum.
explanations.B: Incorrect. hCG is detectable well before a missed period, around the time of implantation roughly six days after conception, which is precisely why early sensitive pregnancy tests work.
explanations.C: Incorrect. hCG is synthesized by the syncytiotrophoblast of the developing placenta, not the corpus luteum; hCG is in fact what rescues the corpus luteum from regression, not the other way round.
explanations.D: Incorrect. hCG shares an identical alpha subunit and a highly homologous beta subunit with pituitary LH, which is why hCG can bind and activate the LH receptor to maintain the corpus luteum.

questions.subject: obs
questions.learning_objective: hCG from the syncytiotrophoblast appears around implantation, about 6 days after conception, and rescues the corpus luteum.

questions.title: Which of the following is an action of progesterone during pregnancy?
questions.question: Which of the following is an action of progesterone during pregnancy?

options.B: Stimulates rhythmic uterine contractions to initiate labor
options.C: Increases the density of myometrial gap junctions and oxytocin receptors

explanations.A: Correct. Progesterone inhibits uterine smooth muscle contractility throughout most of pregnancy, maintaining myometrial quiescence and helping prevent preterm labor. A functional fall in progesterone action near term is thought to help permit the onset of labor.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Stimulating rhythmic contractions to initiate labor is the opposite of progesterone's quiescence-maintaining role; contraction-promoting signals instead come from rising estrogen, prostaglandins, and oxytocin.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Increasing gap junction and oxytocin receptor density is an estrogen-driven change that promotes contractility, opposing rather than reflecting progesterone's action.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cervical ripening and effacement near term are driven mainly by prostaglandins and estrogen; progesterone tends to keep the cervix firm, opposing ripening.

questions.learning_objective: Progesterone maintains myometrial quiescence during pregnancy, opposing uterine contraction.

questions.title: Why is there no significant milk secretion during pregnancy despite high prolactin levels and full mammary gland development?
questions.question: Why is there no significant milk secretion during pregnancy despite high prolactin levels and full mammary gland development?

options.A: High estrogen and progesterone directly inhibit prolactin's action on the breast
options.B: Prolactin receptor expression is completely absent from the mammary gland until after delivery
options.C: Maternal oxytocin levels are too low during pregnancy to permit milk ejection
options.D: The anterior pituitary does not secrete prolactin until parturition

explanations.A: Correct. Despite rising prolactin and full mammary ductal and alveolar development during pregnancy, the very high circulating levels of estrogen and progesterone directly block prolactin's milk-secretory action on the alveolar epithelium. Only after delivery, when placental estrogen and progesterone fall sharply, is this block removed and copious milk secretion begins.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Prolactin receptors are present and are in fact upregulated in the breast during pregnancy (partly under estrogen's influence); the block is at the level of prolactin's downstream action, not receptor absence.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This confuses milk ejection (the let-down reflex, mediated by oxytocin in response to suckling) with milk secretion/synthesis, which is what the question addresses and which is hormonally blocked during pregnancy regardless of oxytocin.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Prolactin rises progressively throughout pregnancy, well before delivery, driven partly by rising estrogen; it is not withheld until parturition.

questions.subject: obs
questions.learning_objective: Antepartum estrogen and progesterone block prolactin's milk-secretory action; their postpartum fall unmasks lactation.

questions.title: Which of the following statements regarding E. coli urinary tract infections is true?
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding E. coli urinary tract infections is true?

options.A: About 90% occur in patients with no underlying anatomical abnormality
options.B: E. coli UTIs occur almost exclusively in patients with a structural urinary tract abnormality
options.C: E. coli is a rare cause of community-acquired UTI
options.D: E. coli UTIs require an indwelling catheter or recent instrumentation in most cases

explanations.A: Correct. E. coli is the leading cause of urinary tract infection, and approximately 90% of these infections are uncomplicated, occurring in patients with a structurally and functionally normal urinary tract, ascending from the periurethral/vaginal flora.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The great majority of E. coli UTIs occur without any underlying structural abnormality; a minority (complicated UTI) occurs in patients with anatomic or functional defects, catheters, or stones.
explanations.C: Incorrect. E. coli is in fact the single most common cause of community-acquired UTI, accounting for the large majority of cases, not a rare one.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Catheterization and instrumentation are risk factors for complicated/catheter-associated UTI, but most E. coli UTIs are uncomplicated community-acquired infections without any device involved.

questions.learning_objective: Most E. coli UTIs are uncomplicated, without an underlying urinary tract abnormality.

questions.title: Which of the following is a true laboratory characteristic of E. coli?
questions.question: Which of the following is a true laboratory characteristic of E. coli?

explanations.A: Correct. E. coli is a gram-negative bacillus of the family Enterobacteriaceae that is oxidase-negative and ferments lactose, producing pink colonies on MacConkey agar — a combination used routinely to distinguish it from oxidase-positive or non-lactose-fermenting gram-negative organisms.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Oxidase-positive, lactose-negative describes organisms such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, not E. coli, which is oxidase-negative and lactose-fermenting.
explanations.C: Incorrect. E. coli is a gram-negative bacillus, not a gram-positive coccus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. E. coli does ferment lactose (it is lactose-positive), unlike non-lactose-fermenting Enterobacteriaceae such as Salmonella and Shigella.

questions.title: A female patient tests positive for VDRL but has no history of syphilis and is asymptomatic. What is the most likely explanation?
questions.question: A female patient tests positive for VDRL but has no history of syphilis and is asymptomatic. What is the most likely explanation?

options.B: This confirms primary syphilis and treatment should begin immediately without further testing
options.C: VDRL is a treponemal-specific confirmatory test that essentially never gives false positives
options.D: This pattern indicates successfully treated past syphilis

explanations.A: Correct. VDRL is a nontreponemal test that can give a biological false-positive result — reacting in the absence of true Treponema pallidum infection — in conditions such as autoimmune disease, pregnancy, or other infections. An unexpected positive VDRL in an asymptomatic patient with no history warrants confirmation with a treponemal-specific test (e.g., FTA-ABS) before diagnosing syphilis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. VDRL is a screening, not confirmatory, test, and an unexpected positive in this clinical context should be confirmed with a treponemal-specific test before treatment, not acted on alone.
explanations.C: Incorrect. VDRL is a nontreponemal (not treponemal-specific) test and is well recognized for producing false positives in a variety of non-syphilitic conditions.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Treponemal-specific tests, not VDRL, typically remain positive for life after treated syphilis; this scenario also has no history of syphilis at all, making past treated infection an unlikely explanation.

questions.subject: inf
questions.learning_objective: An unexpected positive VDRL without supporting history may be a biological false positive, requiring confirmatory treponemal testing.

questions.title: Chancroid is caused by which of the following organisms?
questions.question: Chancroid is caused by which of the following organisms?

explanations.A: Correct. Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi, a gram-negative bacillus that produces painful genital ulcers with ragged, undermined edges and tender, sometimes suppurative, inguinal lymphadenopathy. This painful, ragged ulcer with tender lymphadenopathy contrasts with the classically painless chancre of primary syphilis, a key distinguishing feature in the genital ulcer differential.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Treponema pallidum causes syphilis, whose primary chancre is classically painless, unlike the painful ulcer of chancroid.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Klebsiella granulomatis causes granuloma inguinale (donovanosis), a different chronic, progressive genital ulcer disease.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1-L3 cause lymphogranuloma venereum, characterized more by prominent lymphadenopathy than a persistent ulcer.

questions.title: A male patient with urethritis has a swab showing intracellular gram-negative diplococci. What is the diagnosis?
questions.question: A male patient with urethritis has a swab showing intracellular gram-negative diplococci. What is the diagnosis?

explanations.A: Correct. Intracellular gram-negative diplococci seen within neutrophils on a urethral Gram stain are diagnostic of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, and this finding is sensitive and specific enough in symptomatic men to support presumptive treatment while culture or NAAT confirmation is pending. Chlamydia, by contrast, is diagnosed by nucleic acid amplification testing rather than Gram stain, since it does not appear as visible diplococci.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Chlamydia trachomatis is an obligate intracellular organism that does not Gram stain as visible diplococci; it is diagnosed by nucleic acid amplification testing, not microscopy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Ureaplasma urealyticum lacks a cell wall and therefore does not Gram stain at all, let alone appear as gram-negative diplococci.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Trichomonas vaginalis is a flagellated protozoan identified by its motility on a wet mount preparation, not as gram-negative diplococci on Gram stain.

questions.learning_objective: Intracellular gram-negative diplococci on urethral Gram stain diagnose gonococcal urethritis.

questions.title: Which of the following best indicates latent syphilis?
questions.question: Which of the following best indicates latent syphilis?

options.A: An asymptomatic patient with positive serology and no clinical signs
options.B: A patient with a painless genital chancre and positive serology
options.C: A patient with a diffuse maculopapular rash involving the palms and soles
options.D: A patient with gummatous skin lesions and positive serology

explanations.A: Correct. Latent syphilis is defined by reactive treponemal and nontreponemal serology in a patient who is entirely asymptomatic, with no clinical signs of primary, secondary, or tertiary disease. Latent syphilis still requires staged antibiotic treatment despite the absence of symptoms, in order to prevent progression to tertiary disease.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A painless genital chancre with positive serology describes primary syphilis, which has an overt clinical sign, not the asymptomatic latent stage.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A diffuse maculopapular rash involving the palms and soles is the classic finding of secondary syphilis, a symptomatic stage.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Gummatous skin lesions are a feature of tertiary syphilis, a symptomatic, destructive late stage, not latent (asymptomatic) disease.

questions.subject: inf
questions.learning_objective: Latent syphilis is asymptomatic seroreactivity, without the clinical signs of primary, secondary, or tertiary disease.

questions.title: Which of the following is a diagnostic test used to identify Candida albicans in vaginal candidiasis?
questions.question: Which of the following is a diagnostic test used to identify Candida albicans in vaginal candidiasis?

explanations.A: Correct. The germ tube test is a rapid presumptive identification method in which Candida albicans forms characteristic germ tubes when incubated briefly in serum at 37°C, distinguishing it from most other Candida species. Because it is only presumptive, a positive germ tube test is often followed by culture or further biochemical testing when species-level confirmation is clinically important.
explanations.B: Incorrect. India ink preparation is used to visualize the polysaccharide capsule of Cryptococcus neoformans, not to identify Candida.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The Tzanck smear identifies multinucleated giant cells characteristic of herpesvirus infection, an unrelated fungal-versus-viral distinction.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Darkfield microscopy is used to visualize Treponema pallidum spirochetes in syphilis, not to identify Candida.

questions.title: What is the best regimen for a patient with latent syphilis who is allergic to penicillin?
questions.question: What is the best regimen for a patient with latent syphilis who is allergic to penicillin?

options.B: A single intramuscular dose of benzathine penicillin G despite the allergy
options.C: A single oral dose of azithromycin 1g

explanations.A: Correct. For a non-pregnant, penicillin-allergic patient with late latent syphilis (or latent syphilis of unknown duration), the recommended alternative regimen is oral doxycycline 100mg twice daily for 28 days, an accepted substitute when penicillin, the preferred agent, cannot be used. This regimen substitutes for the preferred benzathine penicillin G when a documented penicillin allergy makes penicillin therapy inappropriate outside of desensitization.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Giving benzathine penicillin despite a documented allergy is contraindicated; the whole premise of this question is finding an appropriate alternative for a penicillin-allergic patient.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A single dose of azithromycin is not a recommended regimen for latent syphilis; resistance and adequacy-of-cure concerns limit azithromycin's role in syphilis treatment.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Syphilis is a bacterial, not viral, infection, so topical antiviral therapy has no role in its treatment.

questions.title: What is the significance of lactic acid-producing bacteria (lactobacilli) normally present in the vagina?
questions.question: What is the significance of lactic acid-producing bacteria (lactobacilli) normally present in the vagina?

options.A: They maintain an acidic vaginal pH that provides natural protection against pathogens
options.B: They are pathogenic commensals that predispose to bacterial vaginosis when present in high numbers
options.C: They raise vaginal pH to alkaline levels
options.D: They have no role in host defense and are simply incidental flora

explanations.A: Correct. Vaginal lactobacilli produce lactic acid, maintaining a normally acidic vaginal pH that inhibits overgrowth of pathogenic bacteria and yeast, an important component of the vagina's natural defense against infection. Loss of this protective lactobacillus-dominated flora and the resulting rise in vaginal pH is what predisposes to overgrowth of anaerobes such as Gardnerella vaginalis in bacterial vaginosis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. It is loss, not overgrowth, of protective lactobacilli that predisposes to bacterial vaginosis, allowing anaerobic organisms such as Gardnerella vaginalis to overgrow as vaginal pH rises.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Lactobacilli lower, not raise, vaginal pH through lactic acid production, which is precisely how they inhibit pathogen overgrowth.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Lactobacilli play an active, protective role in host defense by maintaining an inhospitable acidic environment for pathogens, not a purely incidental one.

questions.learning_objective: Vaginal lactobacilli protect against infection by maintaining an acidic pH via lactic acid production.

questions.title: A woman complains of a fishy-odor vaginal discharge with a grayish, thin, homogeneous quality. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.question: A woman complains of a fishy-odor vaginal discharge with a grayish, thin, homogeneous quality. What is the most likely diagnosis?

explanations.A: Correct. A thin, homogeneous, grayish discharge with a characteristic fishy odor, especially after intercourse, is the classic presentation of bacterial vaginosis, caused by an overgrowth of Gardnerella vaginalis and other anaerobes displacing normal lactobacilli. A positive amine ("whiff") test on adding potassium hydroxide to the discharge further supports this diagnosis over candidiasis or trichomoniasis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Candida albicans classically produces a thick, white, curd-like ("cottage cheese") discharge that is typically odorless, not a thin, fishy-odor grayish discharge.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Trichomonas vaginalis classically produces a frothy, yellow-green, malodorous discharge often with a "strawberry cervix," a different picture from the thin grayish fishy discharge of bacterial vaginosis.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Neisseria gonorrhoeae typically produces a purulent, not grayish/fishy, discharge, and is not the classic cause of this presentation.

questions.learning_objective: A fishy-odor grayish discharge is characteristic of Gardnerella vaginalis-associated bacterial vaginosis.

questions.title: Painful vesicular genital lesions progress to ulcers; a skin smear is taken. Which of the following microscopic findings would be expected?
questions.question: Painful vesicular genital lesions progress to ulcers; a skin smear is taken. Which of the following microscopic findings would be expected?

options.A: Multinucleated giant cells with intranuclear inclusion bodies
options.C: Motile flagellated organisms on a wet mount

explanations.A: Correct. A Tzanck smear (Giemsa or Wright stain) of a herpes simplex virus vesicle or early ulcer classically shows multinucleated giant cells with intranuclear inclusion bodies, reflecting the cytopathic effect of HSV replication. Because the Tzanck smear cannot distinguish HSV from varicella-zoster virus and has only moderate sensitivity, PCR or viral culture is used for definitive confirmation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Intracellular gram-negative diplococci within neutrophils are the finding in gonococcal infection, a bacterial rather than viral process, not seen in HSV lesions.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Motile flagellated organisms on wet mount identify Trichomonas vaginalis, an unrelated protozoan infection.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Spirochetes on darkfield microscopy identify Treponema pallidum in syphilis, a different genital ulcer pathogen from HSV.

questions.subject: inf
questions.learning_objective: Multinucleated giant cells with intranuclear inclusions on Tzanck smear indicate HSV.

questions.title: A pregnant woman at 36 weeks has a positive Group B Streptococcus screening culture. What is the recommended management?
questions.question: A pregnant woman at 36 weeks has a positive Group B Streptococcus screening culture. What is the recommended management?

options.A: IV intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis given during labor
options.B: Oral antibiotics completed antenatally, with no further treatment at labor
options.C: No treatment is needed since GBS is a normal commensal organism
options.D: Elective cesarean section is mandatory for all GBS-positive mothers

explanations.A: Correct. A pregnant woman with a positive Group B Streptococcus screening culture should receive intravenous intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis, typically penicillin G or ampicillin, given during labor. This substantially reduces the risk of neonatal early-onset GBS sepsis and meningitis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A one-time antenatal oral antibiotic course is not adequate because GBS recolonization commonly occurs before delivery; prophylaxis must be given intravenously during labor itself.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Although GBS can be a normal vaginal/rectal commensal, a positive screening culture in pregnancy specifically mandates intrapartum prophylaxis to protect the neonate from early-onset disease.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Vaginal delivery with intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis is standard management; cesarean section is not required for GBS colonization alone.

questions.learning_objective: GBS-positive pregnant women receive IV intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis to prevent neonatal early-onset disease.

questions.title: A newborn develops ophthalmia neonatorum (conjunctivitis) at two weeks of age. What is the most likely causative agent?
questions.question: A newborn develops ophthalmia neonatorum (conjunctivitis) at two weeks of age. What is the most likely causative agent?

explanations.A: Correct. Chlamydial ophthalmia neonatorum typically presents later than gonococcal disease, around 5 to 14 days after birth (and can appear up to several weeks later), making Chlamydia trachomatis the most likely cause of conjunctivitis presenting at two weeks of age. Gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, in contrast, presents earlier, within the first two to five days of life, with a more acute, hyperpurulent discharge.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum typically presents earlier, within the first 2 to 5 days of life, with a more acute, hyperpurulent conjunctivitis, not at two weeks.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Neonatal HSV conjunctivitis or keratitis is less common and usually accompanies other signs of localized skin-eye-mouth or disseminated disease, and is not the classic explanation for isolated conjunctivitis at this age.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Staphylococcus aureus is a less specific and less classically age-timed cause of neonatal conjunctivitis than chlamydia at this particular two-week presentation.

questions.learning_objective: Chlamydial ophthalmia neonatorum classically presents later (around 1-2 weeks) than gonococcal ophthalmia (within days).

questions.title: What is the highest risk to the fetus if maternal rubella infection occurs during the first trimester?
questions.question: What is the highest risk to the fetus if maternal rubella infection occurs during the first trimester?

options.B: Risk is negligible in the first trimester and rises only in the third trimester
options.C: The main risk is maternal, not fetal, morbidity
options.D: The fetus develops passive lifelong immunity with no adverse effects

explanations.A: Correct. First-trimester maternal rubella infection occurs during the period of fetal organogenesis, when the developing heart, eyes, and inner ear are most vulnerable to teratogenic insult, giving the highest risk of congenital rubella syndrome — cardiac defects, cataracts, and sensorineural deafness — of any gestational window. Risk falls progressively with infection later in gestation, which is why documenting rubella immunity before conception is emphasized in preconception care.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The risk of severe congenital malformation is highest, not negligible, with first-trimester infection, and falls progressively with infection later in pregnancy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Maternal rubella infection is typically mild in the mother; the major clinical concern is teratogenic risk to the fetus, not maternal morbidity.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Congenital rubella causes serious, sometimes permanent, organ damage rather than conferring simple, harmless passive immunity to the fetus.

questions.subject: inf
questions.learning_objective: First-trimester maternal rubella infection carries the highest risk of congenital organ defects.

questions.title: A female patient with prolonged rupture of membranes has a neonate who develops late-onset neonatal listeriosis. Which of the following is a possible complication?
questions.question: A female patient with prolonged rupture of membranes has a neonate who develops late-onset neonatal listeriosis. Which of the following is a possible complication?

explanations.A: Correct. Late-onset neonatal listeriosis, typically acquired perinatally around the time of delivery and presenting days after birth, classically involves the central nervous system, with meningitis or meningoencephalitis as its hallmark complication. This CNS tropism is why Listeria monocytogenes is a leading cause of neonatal bacterial meningitis and why empiric neonatal sepsis coverage often includes ampicillin.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Congenital heart defects are not a recognized complication of listeriosis; they are more typically associated with first-trimester teratogenic infections such as rubella.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hemolytic disease of the newborn is an Rh or ABO alloimmunization process, unrelated to Listeria infection.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Neonatal hypothyroidism is not a recognized complication of listeriosis.

questions.learning_objective: Late-onset neonatal listeriosis classically causes meningitis/meningoencephalitis.

questions.title: A recently born baby develops cutaneous skin lesions consistent with neonatal herpes. Which of the following is a possible complication that may develop?
questions.question: A recently born baby develops cutaneous skin lesions consistent with neonatal herpes. Which of the following is a possible complication that may develop?

options.D: Permanent immunity with no further risk of disease

explanations.A: Correct. Neonatal HSV disease that initially presents as localized skin-eye-mouth lesions carries a real risk of progression to central nervous system or disseminated disease, with encephalitis a recognized and serious complication. This is why systemic antiviral therapy is started promptly.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Congenital rubella syndrome is caused by an entirely different virus (rubella), not HSV, and is not a complication of neonatal herpes.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Erythroblastosis fetalis is an Rh-alloimmunization process unrelated to HSV infection.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Neonatal HSV carries a real risk of severe complications, including recurrence, and does not confer simple permanent protective immunity, understating the clinical risk.

questions.subject: inf
questions.learning_objective: Cutaneous neonatal HSV disease can progress to encephalitis, warranting prompt systemic antiviral therapy.

questions.title: Regarding congenital rubella, which of the following statements is true?
questions.question: Regarding congenital rubella, which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The rubella vaccine is live attenuated and is not given during pregnancy
options.B: The rubella vaccine is inactivated and safe to give at any point in pregnancy
options.C: Maternal rubella vaccination during pregnancy has been definitively proven to cause congenital malformations in every documented case
options.D: Postpartum rubella vaccination is contraindicated in breastfeeding mothers

explanations.A: Correct. The rubella vaccine, typically given as the combined MMR vaccine, is a live attenuated vaccine and is therefore not given during pregnancy, particularly not in the first trimester, as a precaution against theoretical fetal infection, even though the vaccine strain has not been definitively shown to cause congenital rubella syndrome. Because of this precaution, rubella immunity is ideally confirmed and any needed vaccination completed before conception, or otherwise given postpartum once the mother has delivered.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The rubella vaccine is live attenuated, not inactivated, and is contraindicated in pregnancy, not safe to give at any point.
explanations.C: Incorrect. This overstates the evidence; the contraindication is precautionary rather than based on definitively proven congenital malformation in every documented case of inadvertent vaccination during pregnancy.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Postpartum rubella vaccination is actually recommended for non-immune mothers and is considered safe during breastfeeding, not contraindicated.

questions.subject: inf
questions.learning_objective: The live attenuated rubella vaccine is avoided in pregnancy as a precaution against fetal infection.

questions.title: In urinary bilharziasis, terminal hematuria occurs at which stage of the parasite's life cycle in the host?
questions.question: In urinary bilharziasis, terminal hematuria occurs at which stage of the parasite's life cycle in the host?

options.A: Stage of egg extrusion through the bladder mucosa
options.C: Stage of migration of schistosomula through the lungs
options.D: Stage of adult worm pairing in the mesenteric venules

explanations.A: Correct. Schistosoma haematobium eggs deposited in the bladder wall are extruded through the mucosa into the lumen to reach the urine. This extrusion causes local mucosal hemorrhage that is most pronounced at the end of micturition, when contraction of the bladder base and trigone — where egg deposition is densest — squeezes out blood, producing the classic terminal hematuria.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cercarial skin penetration is the early infective stage, producing at most a transient local dermatitis (cercarial dermatitis), not urinary tract hematuria.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Pulmonary migration of schistosomula is an early, largely asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic (cough) stage of the life cycle, unrelated to bladder hematuria.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Adult worm pairing occurs in the venous plexus (vesical venules for S. haematobium), a stage that precedes egg deposition and does not itself cause the mucosal bleeding responsible for terminal hematuria.

questions.subject: inf
questions.learning_objective: Terminal hematuria in urinary schistosomiasis results from egg extrusion through the bladder mucosa.

questions.title: In a case of schistosoma infection, how is the intensity of the infection measured?
questions.question: In a case of schistosoma infection, how is the intensity of the infection measured?

options.A: Examination of urine by the filtration method with quantitative egg counting
options.B: A single qualitative wet-mount slide with no counting
options.C: Serum antibody titer alone, without any urine or stool examination

explanations.A: Correct. The intensity of Schistosoma haematobium infection is measured by filtering a fixed volume of urine (commonly 10mL) through a membrane or syringe filter and counting the recovered eggs, expressed as eggs per fixed urine volume — the standard technique used in both clinical assessment and schistosomiasis control programs. This quantitative approach is used both to classify individual infections as light or heavy intensity and to monitor the impact of community-level mass drug administration programs.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A simple qualitative wet mount without counting can detect eggs but does not quantify infection intensity, which requires a standardized filtration and counting method.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Serum antibody testing indicates exposure but does not reliably quantify current egg burden or infection intensity the way direct egg counting does.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Peripheral eosinophilia can accompany schistosomiasis but is a nonspecific finding and not a validated method for measuring infection intensity.

questions.subject: inf
questions.learning_objective: Urine filtration with quantitative egg counting is the standard method for measuring schistosomiasis infection intensity.

questions.title: Swimmer's itch (cercarial dermatitis) is due to which of the following?
questions.question: Swimmer's itch (cercarial dermatitis) is due to which of the following?

options.A: Furcocercous cercariae penetration of the skin
options.B: Deposition of eggs in the dermis
options.C: Migration of adult worms through subcutaneous tissue
options.D: An allergic reaction to schistosome antigens released during treatment

explanations.A: Correct. Swimmer's itch (cercarial dermatitis) results from penetration of the skin by furcocercous (fork-tailed) schistosome cercariae released from infected freshwater snails. The resulting pruritic papular eruption is a local hypersensitivity reaction to the penetrating larvae.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Egg deposition occurs later in the life cycle, within blood vessels of the definitive host's viscera (bladder or intestine), not in the skin, and is not the cause of swimmer's itch.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adult schistosome worms reside in venous plexuses of the viscera, not in subcutaneous tissue, and do not cause this skin reaction.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Swimmer's itch is caused by the initial cercarial penetration event itself, not by an antigen-release reaction during antiparasitic treatment (which describes a different phenomenon, such as a post-treatment inflammatory response).

questions.subject: inf
questions.learning_objective: Swimmer's itch results from furcocercous cercarial skin penetration, a local hypersensitivity reaction.

questions.title: A pregnant female with trichomonas vaginalis infection is at risk of which of the following complications?
questions.question: A pregnant female with trichomonas vaginalis infection is at risk of which of the following complications?

explanations.A: Correct. Trichomonas vaginalis infection during pregnancy is associated with an increased risk of preterm labor, premature rupture of membranes, and low birth weight, an association thought to relate to the local inflammatory response the infection provokes in the genital tract. Recognizing this association supports screening for and treating symptomatic trichomoniasis in pregnancy, alongside its more familiar role as a common cause of vaginal discharge.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Fetal cardiac malformation is a first-trimester teratogenic risk associated with certain viral infections (e.g., rubella), not with trichomoniasis, which is a local vaginal/cervical infection rather than a teratogen.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Molar pregnancy is a gestational trophoblastic disease arising from abnormal fertilization, unrelated to Trichomonas infection.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Trichomoniasis is associated with an increased risk of preterm, not prolonged, labor.
